newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed after early rally fizzles.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed after early rally fizzles.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures shed early gains to end narrowly mixed Thursday, pressured by a bout of local long liquidation and commission house profit taking, traders said.

Buying on the part of commission houses and commodity funds bolstered prices early on, dealers said. Key March ran up this morning, with this most-active contract piercing resistance at 117.50 cents a lb, the high seen the past three consecutive trading days.

March broke through the next technical barrier at 119.00 cents, rising to a high of 119.20 before the buying dried up, prompting players to quickly take profits and the ring to shed their long positions.
"When the buying was done, it was done," a trader said. "The sell-off came because the entire ring was long."
March ended down 0.25 cent at 116.65 cents after trading from 119.20 to 115.50. Second-position May gained 0.20 cent to 114.95, while the rest finished 0.20 firmer to 1.25 lower.

On the charts, March support was seen at 115 cents, followed by 113-112 and 110. Traders said the contract would need to clear 117.50 again to regain upward momentum and breach next resistance level at about 120.
The day's volume was estimated at 7,923 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212 859 1640))
